rationale:
The example `requirements.sdk.graph.hierarchical-paths` gives a concrete case with an expected result. In an illustrative Habeas domain, a `HabeasNodeId::Requirement(vec!["a","b","c"])` identity maps through `node_path` to the path `["requirement","a","b","c"]`. It cites `requirements.sdk.graph.node_path_method`, which requires that the same `NodeId` always gives the same `NodePath`.

The only test, `crates/habeas-sdk/tests/contracts.rs#fn[hierarchical_requirement_identity_maps_each_component_to_a_path_segment]`, reproduces that scenario:
- It defines the same one-variant enum with `Requirement(Vec<String>)`.
- It defines a `node_path` closure that prepends "requirement" to each component and builds a `NodePath` from the result.
- It builds the `a`, `b`, `c` requirement. It asserts that `node_path(...).segments()` equals `["requirement","a","b","c"]`. That checks the expected output.
- It asserts that two conversions of the same identity are equal, which checks the cited determinism rule.

The test does not call a real `Graph::node_path`. The example only sketches how a domain might define its own mapping, so a local mapping that follows the chapter is a fair way to check it. The cited requirement's trait-level behavior is tested elsewhere, in `graph_relationships_work_without_node_contents_or_storage` and `identities_remain_stable_and_fingerprinting_uses_the_supplied_snapshot`. I did not reassess those tests, as the task directs. I found no outcome stated in the example that goes unasserted.
